articles.title: Cyclone Akvan to spare most of Andhra; red alert remains for Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Parvathipuram - The Hindu

articles.full_text:
Fishermen use a tractor to move their boats to safety near Ongole on Wednesday, ahead of Cyclone Akvan.
| Photo Credit: Kommuri Srinivas
Severe cyclonic storm Akvan may not have much impact on Andhra Pradesh, since the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has revised its initial forecast and said isolated extremely heavy rainfall (red alert) is likely only in three districts, Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Parvathipuram Manyam, on Thursday (November 19, 2026).
Earlier, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, Alluri Sitharama Raju and Kakinada were also put on red alert. They have now been put on orange alert for November 19. There are no red alerts for the State on November 20, when the system is likely to cross the coast near Gopalpur in Odisha. But there is an orange alert for Srikakulam and Parvathipuram Manyam on November 20, since isolated very heavy rainfall is likely.
Meanwhile, the system over the west-central Bay of Bengal moved northwards at 15 kmph and was located at 8.30 a.m. over the same region, about 420 km east-southeast of Narsapur, 400 km south-southeast of Kalingapatnam, 490 km south of Gopalpur and 550 km south of Puri in Odisha, and 590 km east-northeast of Chennai.
It is likely to move north-northwestward and cross the north Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and south Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri, close to the east of Gopalpur, by noon on Friday, with a maximum sustained wind speed of 90-100 kmph gusting to 110 kmph.
As of 12 p.m., very light to light showers had begun in Srikakulam district. Ichchapuram recorded 12.5 mm between 8.30 a.m. and noon, the highest in the State, according to the Directorate of Economics and Statistics, Andhra Pradesh (DES-AP). In the 24 hours to 8.30 a.m., no station had recorded more than 9 mm.
Thunderstorms and gales, with speeds reaching 90 to 100 kmph, gusting to 110 kmph, are likely at isolated places in coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam on Thursday. Squally winds of 30-40 kmph may prevail in Rayalaseema.
The intensity of the wind may come down on Friday, since the maximum speed may not go beyond 50 kmph along the coast on November 20, according to the IMD.
Srikakulam, Vizianagaram on high alert
The Srikakulam and Vizianagaram district administrations are on high alert ahead of Cyclone Akvan, which is expected to cross the coast near Gopalpur in Odisha on Friday. Srikakulam, which suffered heavily in the two recent cyclones, Arnab and Murasu, is ready to face the new challenge.
Srikakulam Collector Swapnil Dinakar Pundkar and other officials visited Donkuru and other villages of Ichchapuram, on the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha border, to review the preparedness of local officials. Ichchapuram, Sompeta and other areas were badly affected by floods in the Bahuda after the earlier cyclones.
The Collector told The Hindu that NDRF and SDRF teams would be deployed at sensitive places and people in vulnerable areas would be shifted to safe locations. He said cattle would also be taken care of for the next few days.
Traffic would be regulated on NH-16, the Kolkata-Chennai highway, which was disrupted by floodwater during the earlier cyclones, he said. Wind speeds would be around 60-70 kmph, and moderate to heavy rainfall was likely, according to the IMD’s bulletin, he added.
Vizianagaram Collector S. Ramsundar Reddy reviewed the situation at the coastal villages of Pusapatirega and Bhogapuram and asked officials to take necessary measures ahead of the cyclone. He said fishermen had been advised not to venture into the sea for the next few days on the government’s orders.
Published - November 19, 2026 01:08 pm IST

Growing rain bands (purple and light blue) reached out to cover north Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, West Bengal and Bangladesh coasts on Thursday noon.
| Photo Credit:
www.meteoblue.com
Coastal and adjoining interior areas of north Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, West Bengal and adjoining Bangladesh across the border appear to have come under heavy weather triggered by severe cyclone Akvan over west-central Bay of Bengal by midday today (Thursday).
International weather models project the metropolis of Kolkata may remain cloudy today (Thursday) with a 95 per cent chance for rain and thunderstorms and a maximum temperature hovering around 25℃. Dew point will be around 22.7℃ with an average humidity of 85 per cent. Winds will be 13 km/hr from the north-east.
Night: Cloudy with a 96 per cent chance for rain and thunderstorms. Low temperature around 22℃. Dew point will be around 21.6℃ with an average humidity of 96 per cent. Winds will remain at 13 km/h from the east-northeast.
Rain bands from Akvan may translate into light to moderate rain over Kakinada and Visakhapatnam over north Andhra Pradesh, growing heavier into Brahmapur and Bhubaneshwar in Odisha, Jamshedpur in Jharkhand, and Kolkata in West Bengal and across the border into Khulna, Dhaka and Chattogram in Bangladesh.
Regional Meteorological Centre at Kolkata under India Meteorological Department (IMD) has predicted the possibility of heavy rain, thunderstorms, lightning and squalls for the meteorological subdivision of Gangetic West Bengal that covers the districts of Kolkata, Howrah and Hooghly, among others. Very heavy rain, thunderstorms, lightning and squalls are forecast for tomorrow (Friday) when the cyclone makes a landfall.
The weather may relent from Saturday, though it would remain cloudy. Interestingly, there is no significant weather forecast for the hilly regions of West Bengal and adjoining Sikkim for these three days. The districts falling under the meteorological subdivision Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim include Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Jalpaiguri, Cooch Behar and Malda, among others.

Cyclone Akvan to cross Andhra Pradesh-Odisha coast by Friday noon; IMD issues red alert in 2 districts
PTI
Last Updated:
2 min
Amaravati: Severe cyclonic storm Akvan is likely to cross the North Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and South Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri, close to Gopalpur, by noon on Friday, the IMD said.
To advertise here,
After moving northwards, the system lay over the west-central Bay of Bengal at 2.30 pm on Thursday, about 390 km east-southeast of Narsapur, 320 km south-southeast of Kalingapatnam, 410 km south of Gopalpur, 470 km south of Puri and 610 km east-northeast of Chennai, the India Meteorological Department said in a press release.
"It (Akvan) is likely to move north-northwestward and cross the North Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and South Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri, close to Gopalpur, by noon on November 20, 2026, with maximum sustained wind speeds of 90-100 kmph (and) gusting to 110 kmph," it said.
The system was earlier expected to cross the coast along mid-coastal Andhra Pradesh but subsequently changed course and veered towards North Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.
In view of the cyclone, the IMD issued a red alert for Srikakulam and Vizianagaram districts on Thursday, an orange alert for Parvatipuram Manyam, Alluri Sitaramaraju (ASR) and Anakapalli districts, and a yellow alert for Kakinada.
It forecasts extremely heavy rainfall at isolated places in Srikakulam and Vizianagaram, and heavy to very heavy rainfall in the orange alert districts.
Heavy rainfall is likely at isolated places in Kakinada district, it said.
The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) advised people in North Andhra to remain alert and urged farmers to take precautions while carrying out agricultural activities. Fishermen were advised not to venture into the sea.
A red alert indicates extremely heavy rainfall exceeding 20.44 cm in 24 hours, while an orange alert signifies very heavy rainfall of 11.56 cm to 20.44 cm and a yellow alert signifies heavy rainfall of 6.45 cm to 11.55 cm.

Over 46,700 people in Odisha have been evacuated to safer locations as severe cyclonic storm 'Akvan' over the westcentral Bay of Bengal lay centred about 580 km south of Gopalpur and 640 km south of Puri at 2.30am on Thursday, officials said.
The cyclone is likely to make landfall between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in the eastern state on Friday. A clearer picture of the storm's trajectory and likely impact is expected by Thursday as its speed and direction continue to change, the officials added.
The storm, according to India Meteorological Department (IMD), was also located about 470 km east-southeast of Narsapur and 490 km south-southeast of Kalingapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, and 570 km east-northeast of Chennai.
Deep Dive

"Odisha's south and northern region along with coastal parts is likely to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall and, at places, extremely heavy rainfall on Friday and Saturday," IMD Director General Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said.
The state government stepped up preparedness measures as Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi held a high-level meeting on Wednesday. At least 14 districts – Gajapati, Ganjam, Puri, Khurda, Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapara, Bhadrak, Balasore, Nayagarh, Cuttack, Jajpur, Dhenkanal, Keonjhar and Mayurbhanj – are likely to be affected by the cyclone and associated rainfall.
The government has issued a red alert for 11 districts, with Ganjam, Malkangiri, Rayagada, Koraput and Kalahandi likely to be among the worst affected.
At least 46,701 people have been evacuated so far, while 448 cyclone shelters have been made operational and another 3,000 are being readied, the officials cited above said. Pregnant women, elderly people and children have been prioritised for evacuation, while residents in hilly areas have been asked to move to safer locations in view of the possibility of landslides.
As many as 60 Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) teams and 14 National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams have been deployed for rescue and relief operations.
The chief minister has directed officials to accord the highest priority to ensuring zero casualties and asked ministers and MLAs to coordinate preparedness measures in potentially affected areas. The government has also provided ₹1 crore each as advance assistance to Ganjam and other districts that are likely to be impacted.
Schools and anganwadi centres in nine districts will remain closed on Thursday and Friday in view of the cyclone threat. The State Selection Board (SSB) has also postponed its scheduled recruitment examinations due to the forecast of heavy rainfall over the next two days.
Four senior officials of the Water Resources department have been assigned to monitor river levels and flood risks in different districts from Friday to Sunday and coordinate precautionary measures with the Engineer-in-Chief.

Politics is his core areas of expertise as he closely tracks Odisha's political landscape, including the rise and transformation of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the Biju Janata Dal (BJD), the two principal political parties in Odisha. His long association with the state's political establishment enables him to write on contemporary developments in a larger political context.
Mohanty takes a deep interest in writing human interest stories, environmental issues and documenting the impact of cyclones, floods, heatwaves, and other climate-related events in one of the most disaster-prone states. His coverage extends to public health, governance reforms and stories on accountability of government institutions.

Cyclone Akvan Alert: Red Alert for Heavy Rain in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, Dense Fog Warning for Delhi, Punjab and Haryana
India is witnessing contrasting weather conditions as severe cyclonic storm Akvan moves closer to the eastern coastline, threatening parts of southern and eastern India with extremely heavy rainfall …
India is witnessing contrasting weather conditions as severe cyclonic storm Akvan moves closer to the eastern coastline, threatening parts of southern and eastern India with extremely heavy rainfall and strong winds. At the same time, northern states are preparing for colder mornings and reduced visibility, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) warning of dense fog in parts of Delhi, Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh.
According to the IMD's November 19 forecast, Akvan is moving northwards over the west-central Bay of Bengal. Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Odisha are among the regions facing the highest rainfall risk. The weather department has warned of extremely heavy showers in isolated areas, while strong winds and rough sea conditions are expected along the coast.
Cyclone Akvan May Make Landfall on November 20
The IMD reported that severe cyclonic storm Akvan was positioned over the west-central Bay of Bengal at 5:30 am on November 19. At that time, it was approximately 440 km east-southeast of Narsapur, 440 km south-southeast of Kalingapatnam and around 530 km south of Gopalpur.
The storm is forecast to move towards the coast and cross between Machilipatnam and Puri around noon on November 20. The expected landfall zone includes the North Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coast, along with South Odisha.
The system is likely to cross the coast as a severe cyclonic storm, with sustained wind speeds of 90–100 kmph and gusts reaching 110 kmph.
The landfall remains a forecast, and the actual timing, location and intensity will depend on the storm's movement. Residents in the coastal districts have been advised to follow official weather bulletins and local administration instructions.
Andhra Pradesh and Odisha Face Extremely Heavy Rainfall Risk
Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Odisha are expected to experience the most significant impact from the approaching storm. The IMD has forecast isolated extremely heavy rainfall in these regions on November 19 and 20.
Some locations could receive more than 204.4 mm of rain within 24 hours. Such intense rainfall may lead to waterlogging, disruption of road transport and flooding in low-lying areas.
Strong winds could also damage trees, electric poles, temporary structures and weak buildings. Coastal communities have been advised to remain alert, particularly in areas vulnerable to flooding and storm-related damage.
Sea conditions are expected to remain rough to very rough along parts of the Odisha and Andhra Pradesh coasts. Fishermen have been warned against venturing into the affected parts of the Bay of Bengal.
West Bengal Also Likely to Receive Heavy Rain
The impact of Akvan is expected to extend beyond Andhra Pradesh and Odisha. Parts of Gangetic West Bengal may experience widespread rainfall, thunderstorms and strong winds over the coming days.
The districts of Purba Medinipur, Paschim Medinipur, South 24 Parganas, Howrah, Jhargram and Bankura are among the areas likely to receive heavy rainfall between November 19 and 21.
Kolkata may also witness thunderstorms accompanied by rain and gusty winds. Residents have been advised to remain cautious during periods of intense rainfall and avoid unnecessary travel in areas prone to waterlogging.
Rainfall activity is also expected in parts of Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Telangana and the northeastern region, although the intensity and timing may vary from one area to another.
Dense Fog Warning for Delhi, Punjab and Haryana
While coastal states prepare for heavy rain, northern India is beginning to experience colder weather conditions. The IMD has warned of dense fog at isolated places in Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh and Delhi on November 19.
Delhi may experience mist or shallow fog during the morning, followed by mainly clear skies. The maximum temperature is expected to remain around 24–26 degrees Celsius, while the minimum may range between 11 and 13 degrees Celsius.
Fog could reduce visibility on roads and affect early-morning travel. Drivers have been advised to reduce speed, use fog lights where necessary and maintain a safe distance from other vehicles.
Parts of Punjab and Haryana may also experience poor visibility during the morning and night. Commuters and passengers travelling by road or rail should check the latest updates before beginning their journeys.
Fishermen Advised to Stay Away From the Sea
The approaching cyclone is expected to make sea conditions particularly dangerous over parts of the west-central, south-western, east-central and north-western Bay of Bengal.
Strong winds and high waves can pose serious risks to fishing boats and other small vessels. The IMD has advised fishermen not to venture into the affected sea areas.
Those already at sea should follow safety instructions and return to safer locations wherever possible. Coastal residents should also avoid visiting beaches and exposed shorelines during periods of rough weather.
Safety Measures for Residents in Vulnerable Areas
With heavy rainfall and strong winds expected near the landfall zone, residents of coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha should remain alert to warnings issued by local authorities.
People living in low-lying areas should follow evacuation instructions if issued. They should avoid crossing flooded roads, stay away from damaged electrical infrastructure and remain indoors during strong winds.
During thunderstorms, people should avoid open fields, isolated trees and waterlogged areas. Emergency supplies, essential medicines, drinking water and charged mobile phones can help households prepare for temporary disruptions.
The immediate focus remains on the movement and intensity of Cyclone Akvan ahead of its expected landfall on November 20. While the eastern coast faces the threat of heavy rain and damaging winds, northern India must prepare for fog-related travel disruptions as winter conditions gradually strengthen.
